Personality: Pacuvius Calavius, a prominent figure of the Calavii, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Pacuvius Calavius owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Calavii. Historical Record: The leading noble of Capua, married to a daughter of Appius Claudius. Proud of Capua, the second city of Italy, he resents Roman overlordship and would bring his city over to whichever power promised it the first place in Italy, as long as its senate keeps its power over the mob. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
